title: TypeScript Repository Architectural Map
objective: Transform the existing safe deterministic repository inventory into a deterministic machine-readable architectural map of the TypeScript codebase so the River Development Agent can reason from actual module relationships rather than path inventory alone.

problem.provenExistingCapability: Repository discovery deterministically inventories, normalizes, classifies, and protects repository paths.
problem.provenGap: Production code has no demonstrated dependency graph, import graph, symbol graph, architecture map, call graph, or impact-analysis capability.
problem.graduationRequirement: The Agent must be able to identify TypeScript modules and their direct architectural relationships before higher-level planning or autonomous change generation can be considered grounded.

architecture.sourceOfRepositoryScope: Existing repository discovery remains authoritative for safe repository scope and protected-path behavior.
architecture.analysisBoundary: Analyze discovered TypeScript source files only; do not independently traverse protected or denied repository paths.
architecture.parser: Use the already-available TypeScript compiler API when resolvable; do not add a new parser dependency merely for this capability.
architecture.modules: Produce deterministic normalized module records keyed by repository-relative path.
architecture.imports: Extract static TypeScript import declarations and export-from declarations, preserving raw module specifiers and resolving repository-local relationships when deterministically possible.
architecture.exports: Extract top-level named export declarations sufficient to expose module API shape without executing source code.
architecture.dependencies: For each analyzed module, expose deterministic direct repository-local dependencies.
architecture.dependents: Derive deterministic reverse direct dependents from resolved local dependencies.
architecture.entryPoints: Expose deterministic entry-point signals from known project/configuration structure and zero-dependent/root characteristics without claiming semantic certainty that cannot be proven.
architecture.impact: Given one or more repository-relative module paths, compute direct dependents as the first bounded impact primitive; transitive impact is not required by UNDERSTAND-001 unless naturally safe and deterministic.
architecture.unresolvedImports: Preserve unresolved or external import specifiers explicitly rather than inventing repository targets.
architecture.determinism: Equivalent repository state must produce deeply equal architectural maps.
architecture.safety: No source execution, repository mutation, package installation, network access, secret traversal, authorization creation, command execution, commit, or push.
architecture.integration: This capability is factual architectural substrate. It must not be represented as autonomous reasoning, planning, or implementation intelligence.
architecture.extensibility: Design the result so later UNDERSTAND capabilities can add symbol relationships, semantic classification, transitive impact, and objective relevance without replacing this primitive.

invariants: Repository discovery remains the safe scope authority.
Protected and denied paths are never independently traversed by architectural analysis.
No module specifier is silently treated as a local dependency unless it resolves deterministically to a discovered TypeScript module.
Architecture analysis never executes repository source code.
Module, import, export, dependency, dependent, entry-point, and impact outputs are deterministically ordered.
External and unresolved imports remain visible rather than being discarded or guessed.
The architectural map is evidence about repository structure, not authorization to mutate it.
No new execution/governance foundation is introduced by this capability.
acceptance: A fixture containing multiple TypeScript modules produces deterministic module records.
Static relative imports resolve to discovered repository-local modules.
Export-from relationships participate in dependency mapping.
External package imports remain explicit and unresolved as repository-local dependencies.
Named top-level exports are reported deterministically.
Reverse direct dependents are derived correctly.
Direct impact for a changed module identifies its immediate dependent modules.
Protected paths remain excluded according to existing repository-discovery scope.
Repeated analysis of unchanged repository state is deeply equal.
Malformed or unsupported source syntax fails or degrades explicitly without executing source code or inventing relationships.
Complete River Development Agent regression passes.
